title: George Washington – the First President
credits: Kelly Jean Kelly and Steve Ember reported this story for VOA Learning English. Jill Robbins adapted it for Learning English.

sentences.en: George Washington was the first president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿是美国第一任总统。

sentences.en: He served from 1789 to 1797.
sentences.zh: 他从1789年任职至1797年。

sentences.en: He was a famous general who led the American colonists to freedom from British rule and he presided over the convention that created the U.S. Constitution.
sentences.zh: 他是一位著名的将领，领导美国殖民者摆脱了英国的统治，并主持了制定美国宪法的会议。

sentences.en: He wanted to retire from public service and return home.
sentences.zh: 他想要退出公职，回到家中。

sentences.en: But the country’s founders wanted him to move to New York and serve as the American president.
sentences.zh: 但国家的缔造者们希望他迁往纽约，担任美国总统。

sentences.en: Washington accepted the job as his duty.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿把这份职务视为自己的职责而接受下来。

sentences.en: Washington was sworn in as president in 1789.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿于1789年宣誓就任总统。

sentences.en: He had to invent the job of being president for all future presidents.
sentences.zh: 他必须为日后的所有总统开创总统这一职务。

sentences.en: He established a group of advisors — called the cabinet—as well as the nation’s official money.
sentences.zh: 他组建了一个被称为内阁的顾问团体，并确立了国家的官方货币。

sentences.en: He appointed a six-member Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他任命了由六名法官组成的最高法院。

sentences.en: And he created the Department of Foreign Affairs, now called the State Department.
sentences.zh: 他还设立了负责外交事务的部门，即现在的国务院。

sentences.en: He hoped to act in such a way that future presidents could continue to build on what he began.
sentences.zh: 他希望自己的行为能够让未来的总统在他所开创的事业基础上继续发展。

sentences.en: From the beginning, George Washington was careful to establish a good working relationship with Congress.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，乔治·华盛顿就谨慎地致力于与国会建立良好的工作关系。

sentences.en: By his actions, he confirmed the separation of powers of the three branches of the government, as described in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 通过他的行动，他确立了宪法所规定的政府三权分立。

sentences.en: Historian Joseph Ellis says one of the best things about George Washington was his ability to give up power.
sentences.zh: 历史学家约瑟夫·埃利斯表示，乔治·华盛顿最出色的品质之一，是他能够交出手中的权力。

sentences.en: At the end of the Revolutionary War, General Washington returned his sword.
sentences.zh: 独立战争结束时，华盛顿将军交还了他的佩剑。

sentences.en: And at the end of his second term, President Washington simply returned home.
sentences.zh: 而在第二任期结束时，华盛顿总统 simply 回到了家中。

sentences.en: Like many plantation owners, Washington was a slave holder.
sentences.zh: 和许多种植园主一样，华盛顿也是一名奴隶主。

sentences.en: By the end of his life, Washington opposed slavery.
sentences.zh: 到晚年时，华盛顿反对奴隶制。

sentences.en: He left a will ordering his survivors to free his slaves after his wife’s death.
sentences.zh: 他在遗嘱中下令，在其妻子去世后释放他的奴隶。

sentences.en: Three years after he finished his second term as president, Washington fell ill.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿完成第二个总统任期三年后，病倒了。

sentences.en: On December 14, 1799, he died in his bed, surrounded by his wife, enslaved maids, and friends.
sentences.zh: 1799年12月14日，他在睡梦中离世，身边围绕着妻子、被奴役的女仆和朋友。

sentences.en: He was 67.
sentences.zh: 他享年67岁。

sentences.en: I’m Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

glossary.def: to formally oversee a meeting or office
a major part of a government with powers and responsibilities that are different from other parts
a legal document in which a person states who should receive his or her possessions after he or she dies
